+# Specora
+
+**AI-Native ITSM Platform**
+
+Specora is an open-source, AI-first ITSM platform built to eventually displace legacy suites like ServiceNow. It treats AI agents and graph relationships as first-class citizens, with a conversational-first interface and a graph-native implementation of the CSDMv5 data model.
+
+## Phase 1: The Kernel
+
+Phase 1 establishes the graph-native CSDMv5 data layer, the API, the foundational GUI, and the event-processing worker.
+
+## Technology Stack
+
+| Layer | Technology |
+|-------|------------|
+| **Monorepo** | pnpm workspaces + Turborepo |
+| **API** | TypeScript, Fastify, GraphQL Yoga, neo4j-driver, grpc-js |
+| **Web GUI** | Next.js 14 (App Router), React Flow, TanStack Query |
+| **Worker** | Python 3.12, asyncio, grpcio, neo4j Python driver |
+| **Graph DB** | Neo4j Community Edition |
+| **Queue / Ops DB** | PostgreSQL 16 |
+| **Inter-service** | gRPC + Protobuf |
+| **Auth** | JWT (stateless) |
+| **Local Dev** | Docker Compose |
+| **Production** | Railway (Docker-based) |
+
+## Directory Structure
+
+```
+specora2/
+├── apps/
+│   ├── api/                    # Fastify API Server
+│   ├── web/                    # Next.js Frontend
+│   └── worker/                 # Python gRPC Worker
+├── packages/
+│   ├── core/                   # Shared TS types, Zod schemas
+│   ├── db/                     # Neo4j schema, migrations, seeders
+│   ├── protobuf/               # .proto definitions + scripts
+│   ├── tsconfig/               # Shared TS configs
+│   └── eslint-config/          # Shared lint rules
+├── docker-compose.yml
+├── turbo.json
+└── pnpm-workspace.yaml
+```
+
+## CSDMv5 Graph Schema (Phase 1 Subset)
+
+### Node Labels
+- `ConfigurationItem` (base)
+- `BusinessService`
+- `ApplicationService`
+- `TechnicalService`
+- `Server`
+- `Database`
+- `Application`
+- `NetworkGear`
+- `User`
+- `Group`
+- `Location`
+
+### Relationship Types
+- `PART_OF`
+- `DEPENDS_ON`
+- `HOSTED_ON`
+- `MANAGED_BY`
+- `OWNED_BY`
+- `LOCATED_AT`
+
+## Development
+
+### Prerequisites
+- Node.js >= 20
+- pnpm >= 8
+- Python 3.12
+- Docker & Docker Compose
+
+### Local Setup
+
+```bash
+# Install dependencies
+pnpm install
+
+# Start infrastructure (Neo4j + Postgres)
+docker-compose up -d neo4j postgres
+
+# Seed Neo4j schema and sample data
+pnpm --filter @specora/db seed
+
+# Start all apps in dev mode
+pnpm dev
+```
+
+The API will be available at `http://localhost:4000/graphql` and the web UI at `http://localhost:3000`.
+
+### Proto Generation
+
+```bash
+pnpm proto:generate
+```
+
+## Keyboard Shortcuts
+
+- `Ctrl+K` / `Cmd+K` — Open Specora Assistant chat overlay from anywhere in the UI.
+
+## License
+
+AGPL-3.0
+

Phase 2 candidates based on typical ITSM platform development:

Great question. Phase 1 gave us a solid testing & validation foundation. The natural next question is: **what's the highest-leverage capability to build next?**

Here are the most compelling Phase 2 candidates, ordered by impact vs. complexity:

---

### Option A: Conversational AI Tier 2 — "Agentic CMDB"
Make the chat actually *do* things. Right now it just calls OpenAI with a generic prompt. Next level:
- **Tool-calling**: give the LLM tools to query Neo4j (`search_cis`, `get_service_map`, `create_ci`), execute them, and stream results back
- **Streaming responses**: switch from blocking `chat.completions.create` to SSE streams in the UI
- **Conversation persistence**: store chat history in Postgres, scoped to users
- **Context-aware grounding**: inject relevant CI subgraph context into the system prompt before responding

*Why now:* The UI already has a chat overlay (Ctrl+K). Making it actually useful is high-demo-value.

---

### Option B: Graph Visualization Tier 2 — "Real Data, Real Interactions"
The React Flow graph is currently static/mock. Next level:
- **Wire GraphQL queries**: fetch actual CIs and relationships from Neo4j, render them
- **Node detail panels**: click a node to see attributes, relationships, edit inline
- **Relationship editing**: drag-to-connect nodes, validate against the allowlist
- **Impact analysis**: highlight downstream dependency chains on selection

*Why now:* The frontend's main view is the graph explorer. Without real data it's just wallpaper.

---

### Option C: CMDB Ingestion Pipeline — "Real Data In"
The `ingestCMDB` gRPC endpoint exists but the pipeline is minimal. Next level:
- **CSV/JSON bulk upload API**: multipart upload, validate rows against Zod schemas
- **Async job tracking**: the worker already polls Postgres jobs — actually use it for ingestion
- **Deduplication**: fuzzy match incoming CIs against existing nodes before merge
- **Ingestion UI**: drag-and-drop upload with progress in the web app

*Why now:* An empty CMDB is useless. This gets real customer data flowing in.

---

### Option D: Auth & RBAC Hardening
The auth layer is JWT + basic login. Next level:
- **Password reset flow**: email tokens (could mock with console log in dev)
- **Role-based access control**: `admin`, `analyst`, `viewer` roles, decorate resolvers with `@requireRole`
- **API key authentication**: for service-to-service / integration use cases
- **Session management**: token refresh, revoke

*Why now:* Security is foundational. But maybe less exciting than user-facing features.

---

### Option E: Search & Discovery
Add a real search layer:
- **Full-text index**: Neo4j full-text search over CI names, classes, attributes
- **Global search bar**: Cmd+Shift+K or similar to jump to any CI
- **Faceted filters**: by class, environment, owner, relationship depth

*Why now:* ITSM power users live in search. Fast discovery is a core differentiator.

---

**My recommendation:** Stack **A + B** together. The chat becomes the "input" layer (create/update via conversation) and the graph becomes the "output" layer (see what changed). They're complementary and both lean heavily on the Neo4j layer we just hardened.

**What resonates with you?** Or do you want to tackle something else entirely (observability, performance, multi-tenancy, integrations)?

---

### Option A: Agentic Chat Architecture

**Core decision: where does tool execution live?**

Three approaches:

| Approach | Pros | Cons |
|----------|------|------|
| **A1: Tool definitions in `@specora/core`, execution in `apps/api/services/chat.ts`** | Single request/response cycle, simple to test, no extra latency | API becomes stateful during multi-turn tool loops, harder to stream |
| **A2: Separate `ChatAgent` service class that the chat route calls** | Clean separation, reusable for other entry points (Slack, email) | More boilerplate |
| **A3: Streaming via SSE/WebSocket, tool loop on the backend** | Best UX (typewriter effect), handles long tool chains gracefully | More complex frontend state management |

**My recommendation:** Start with **A1** (execute in `chat.ts`), but structure it so the tool definitions are pure functions that return `{ name, parameters, execute }` objects. This makes it trivial to migrate to A2/A3 later without rewriting tool logic.

**Key schema additions:**
```ts
// @specora/core — new schemas
const ToolCallSchema = z.object({
  tool: z.enum(["search_cis", "get_ci", "create_ci", "update_ci", "get_service_map"]),
  params: z.record(z.any()),
});

const ChatMessageSchema = z.object({
  role: z.enum(["user", "assistant", "tool"]),
  content: z.string(),
  tool_calls: z.array(ToolCallSchema).optional(),
});
```

**OpenAI function-calling flow:**
1. User sends message
2. Backend injects system prompt + available tools schema
3. OpenAI may respond with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`
4. Backend executes each tool against Neo4j, appends results as `role: "tool"` messages
5. Re-send to OpenAI with tool results
6. Return final assistant message (or stream it)

**Streaming:** For Phase 2A MVP, I'd skip SSE and do blocking responses. We can add streaming in a fast follow without architectural breakage.

---

### Option D: RBAC Architecture

The key question is **where roles live**. Options:

| Approach | Storage | Pros | Cons |
|----------|---------|------|------|
| **D1: Roles as Neo4j node properties** (`User:ConfigurationItem {roles: ["admin"]}`) | Already have user nodes | Zero schema changes | Hard to query membership, no expiration |
| **D2: Roles in JWT claims** (`{ sub: "usr-1", roles: ["admin"] }`) | Stateless | Fastest auth checks | Token bloat, need re-login to refresh roles |
| **D3: Postgres roles table + middleware decorator** | New table | Most flexible, audit trail | Extra query per request |

**My recommendation:** **D2 for the JWT payload + D3 for the source of truth**. Store roles in a Postgres `user_roles` table, look them up at login time, embed in JWT. The `@fastify/jwt` plugin already gives us `request.user` — we just add a `roles` field.

```ts
// apps/api/src/plugins/jwt.ts — extend
fastify.decorate("authorize", (roles: string[]) => {
  return async (request: FastifyRequest, reply: FastifyReply) => {
    const user = request.user as { id: string; roles: string[] };
    if (!roles.some(r => user.roles?.includes(r))) {
      reply.status(403).send({ error: "Forbidden" });
    }
  };
});
```

Then decorate resolvers:
```ts
// GraphQL
onRequest: [fastify.authenticate, fastify.authorize(["admin", "analyst"])],
```

---

**Questions for you:**

1. From the Grok chat — did you land on function-calling vs. text-based tool parsing (where the LLM outputs JSON in markdown and you regex it out)? I strongly recommend native OpenAI function calling.

2. For RBAC — do you need **resource-level** permissions (e.g., "Alice can edit CIs in the Prod environment but only view Staging") or just **global roles** (admin/analyst/viewer)? Resource-level is significantly more complex and probably overkill for Phase 2.

3. Conversation persistence — do you want chat history stored in **Postgres** (structured, queryable) or **Neo4j** (could model conversation → message → tool_call graph)? I'd default to Postgres.

Paste the Grok discussion and I'll give you specific feedback on where I agree/disagree with the recommendations!

[&amp;_h2:not(.not-prose):first-child]:mt-0 [&amp;_h3:not(.not-prose):first-child]:mt-0 [&amp;_h4:not(.not-prose):first-child]:mt-0"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">The idea is <strong class="font-semibold">strong</strong> and timely—potentially a smart way to attack a massive, entrenched market from a modern, developer- and user-friendly angle. ServiceNow dominates ITSM and enterprise service management with roughly 44% market share in many segments, boasting a highly integrated platform centered on its <strong class="font-semibold">CMDB</strong> (Configuration Management Database) as the single source of truth for assets, dependencies, services, and workflows.<a href="https://lovable.dev/guides/jira-vs-servicenow-itsm-comparison" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow" class="no-copy inline text-nowrap print:hidden py-[2.5px] ps-2 pe-2 rounded-full align-[0.5px] bg-surface-l1 text-[13px] leading-none font-medium !text-fg-secondary hover:!text-fg-primary visited:text-fg-secondary focus:outline-none !no-underline hover:!no-underline citation" data-state="closed">⁠Lovable</a></p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Their revenue continues growing (on track toward $15B+ by 2026 in some forecasts), and they've aggressively layered on AI via <strong class="font-semibold">Now Assist</strong>, AI agents, predictive intelligence, and an AI Control Tower. Yet the platform remains notoriously complex, expensive (high subscription + implementation costs, often requiring consultants and dedicated admins), slow to deploy (9-18 months for full enterprise rollouts), and form-heavy rather than conversational.</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Your approach—<strong class="font-semibold">AI-first</strong>, <strong class="font-semibold">chat interface-first</strong>, <strong class="font-semibold">GraphQL-based CMDB</strong> as the foundational layer for a broader service delivery platform—directly targets those pain points while riding 2026 trends:</p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Key Strengths of Your Idea</h3>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Chat-first UX</strong>: This aligns perfectly with where work happens today (Slack/Teams, natural language requests). Employees and agents already expect conversational interfaces; bolting chat onto legacy forms feels clunky. True chat-native systems (some emerging alternatives emphasize this) reduce context-switching and speed resolution. ServiceNow has conversational elements, but they're not the default "first" experience.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">AI as the core (not a bolt-on)</strong>: Modern alternatives are pushing <strong class="font-semibold">agentic AI</strong>—autonomous agents that triage, resolve, or orchestrate across incidents, changes, assets, etc., using the CMDB as context. Building AI-native means your system can reason over the graph of dependencies proactively (e.g., "This change will impact these services—simulate impact?"). ServiceNow's AI is powerful but layered on a traditional architecture; a from-scratch AI-first design could feel more fluid and require less human oversight for routine work.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">GraphQL CMDB</strong>: Excellent technical choice for a modern baseline. GraphQL excels at flexible, efficient querying—clients fetch exactly the data needed without over/under-fetching, which is ideal for a rich, relational CMDB (CIs, relationships, service maps, business context). It makes the platform more developer-friendly for integrations, custom apps, and extensions compared to ServiceNow's more proprietary data model (though they have CSDM). This could lower the barrier for building a true "service delivery platform" on top—extending beyond ITSM into HR, facilities, security, etc., via a composable graph.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Baseline layer strategy</strong>: Positioning the CMDB + GraphQL API as the neutral, extensible foundation (the "Switzerland" for data and workflows) lets you avoid full rip-and-replace battles initially. Enterprises hate vendor lock-in on AI models or workflows; a clean, queryable foundation could integrate with existing tools while enabling faster value from AI agents. Some discussions even question if traditional CMDBs are "dead" in highly dynamic cloud environments, favoring more flexible data lakes or graphs—your approach could modernize that.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Overall, this has real disruption potential in a market where customers complain about ServiceNow's complexity, cost, and implementation timelines. Mid-market or agile enterprises (or those frustrated with legacy deployments) could adopt faster. The broader service delivery angle opens doors to enterprise service management (ESM) beyond pure IT.</p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Realistic Challenges</h3>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">Data accuracy and population</strong>: The hardest part of any CMDB isn't the tech—it's keeping it accurate and populated in real-time across hybrid/cloud/on-prem environments. ServiceNow's Discovery and Service Mapping are mature (though not perfect). You'll need strong automated discovery, reconciliation, and governance from day one, or the AI/chat layer will hallucinate or give bad advice due to stale context. Integration with clouds, SCCM, etc., will be non-trivial.</p></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">Enterprise trust and scale</strong>: Big organizations demand reliability, auditability, compliance (ITIL alignment, security, SOC2, etc.), and proven ROI. ServiceNow wins on the "single platform" moat with deep process orchestration. A new entrant must prove the CMDB can handle massive scale without data drift and that AI agents deliver measurable deflection/automation without constant tuning.</p></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">Competition is heating up</strong>: ServiceNow isn't standing still—they're pushing AI agents hard. Alternatives include:</p><ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">AI-native/agentic players</strong> like Rezolve.ai, Atomicwork, or others built around agents from the ground up.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Lighter/faster options like Freshservice, Jira Service Management (strong in DevOps/Atlassian ecosystems), or Salesforce Agentforce (chat/Slack-heavy with AI agents).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">CMDB-focused tools (Device42, Virima, etc.) or visual/automated alternatives.</li>
</ul><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Many emphasize quicker time-to-value and lower TCO. Your differentiator (pure chat + GraphQL + AI-first) needs to be crisp.</p></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">Go-to-market hurdles</strong>: Sales cycles for enterprise service platforms are long. You'll compete on total cost of ownership (TCO), implementation speed, and ecosystem (integrations, partners). Open GraphQL APIs help with extensibility, but you'll still need robust connectors and perhaps low-code/no-code on top for non-dev users.</p></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">CMDB isn't sexy on its own</strong>: As a "baseline layer," it risks being invisible. Success depends on how compelling the chat/AI experiences are on top—e.g., natural language queries like "Show me dependencies for this service and simulate a failure," with proactive recommendations.</p></li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">My Overall Take</h3>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">I like it a lot. The market is ripe for a <strong class="font-semibold">modern, lightweight, intelligent alternative</strong> that feels like "ServiceNow for the AI/chat era"—faster to adopt, more intuitive, and built for agentic workflows rather than retrofitted. GraphQL as the query layer is a clever foundation for flexibility and performance. If you nail accurate, real-time CMDB population + truly autonomous-yet-governed AI agents via chat, you could carve out significant share, especially with organizations tired of million-dollar implementations.</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Execution will be key: prioritize discovery/reconciliation early, focus on measurable outcomes (ticket deflection, MTTR reduction, easier extensions), and consider starting with a strong vertical or mid-market wedge before full enterprise plays. Trends favor conversational + AI-native designs, so the timing feels right.</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">What stage are you at (MVP, architecture decisions, specific tech stack)? Any particular focus area (e.g., cloud-heavy environments, specific integrations)? I'd be happy to brainstorm more on the data model, AI agent patterns, or differentiation strategies. This space needs fresh thinking—good luck!</p></div></div><section class="inline-media-container flex flex-col gap-1 clear-both"></section></div></div><div class="order-first sticky hidden [&amp;_h2:not(.not-prose):first-child]:mt-0 [&amp;_h3:not(.not-prose):first-child]:mt-0 [&amp;_h4:not(.not-prose):first-child]:mt-0"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">That's a solid MVP foundation—<strong class="font-semibold">visually compelling</strong>, <strong class="font-semibold">developer-friendly</strong>, and aligned with the AI/chat-first vision. The <strong class="font-semibold">ReactFlow canvas</strong> as the primary landing page for exploring CMDB relationships gives an immediate "wow" factor that ServiceNow's more tabular/forms-heavy experience lacks. Ctrl+K chat as the quick-access command center feels natural (like modern IDEs or Raycast/Spotlight), and the <strong class="font-semibold">macOS-style dock</strong> with pluggable apps + all-apps menu creates an extensible, app-like desktop experience inside the browser. Exposing the CMDB graph as the shared data layer to plugins (incident, change, problem, knowledge, etc.) while letting those plugins contribute specialized agents is a smart composable architecture.</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">This setup positions your platform as a <strong class="font-semibold">true baseline layer</strong>: the graph handles relationships and context, plugins add domain-specific logic and agents, and everything surfaces through natural language + visual exploration. It's more modern than most 2026 competitors, which often bolt AI onto legacy structures.</p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">What Works Really Well Here</h3>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Visual-first CMDB entry point</strong>: ReactFlow shines for interactive node/edge graphs. Custom nodes can represent CIs with rich details (status, health, ownership, impact score), and edges can encode relationship types (depends_on, runs_on, etc.). This makes dependency mapping and impact analysis intuitive—users can zoom, pan, filter, or even simulate changes directly on the canvas. Many CMDB visualizations struggle with clutter at scale, so starting here differentiates you.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Chat as the universal interface</strong>: Ctrl+K + OpenAI integration is a great start. With keyword linking to specialized agents (e.g., @incident for triage, @change for risk simulation), it turns the chat into an orchestrator that reasons over the full graph. This agentic pattern—where agents use the CMDB as universal context—mirrors what top AI-native players like Rezolve.ai or Atomicwork emphasize: agents that plan, act, and coordinate across modules rather than isolated chatbots.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Pluggable architecture</strong>: The dock + plugins model lowers barriers for extensions. Plugins expose their own agents and data slices while everything stays grounded in the shared GraphQL CMDB. This supports your broader service delivery platform goal (ITSM → ESM) without monolithic bloat. It also feels extensible for third-party developers or internal teams building custom apps.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">GraphQL as the backbone</strong>: Perfect for flexible queries over a rich, relational graph. Clients (ReactFlow canvas, chat resolvers, plugin UIs) can request exactly the subgraphs they need, reducing over-fetching and enabling performant real-time updates.</li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Potential Rough Edges &amp; Suggestions to Level It Up</h3>
<ol dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">Performance at Enterprise Scale</strong>
ReactFlow graphs can lag with hundreds/thousands of nodes if not optimized. Common fixes include:</p><ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Wrap custom nodes/edges in <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">React.memo</span>.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Use local state where possible and avoid global re-renders on every drag/zoom.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Implement virtualization or "only render visible nodes" strategies.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">For very large graphs, consider hybrid approaches (e.g., aggregate clusters or use layout algorithms from libraries like yFiles for better auto-layout).</li>
</ul><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Test early with realistic CMDB sizes (e.g., 10k+ CIs with relationships).</p></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">Data Quality &amp; Population (The Eternal CMDB Challenge)</strong>
The canvas and agents are only as good as the underlying data. Stale or incomplete CIs kill trust fast. In 2026, competitors stress automated discovery, reconciliation, and real-time sync. Prioritize:</p><ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Strong ingestion pipelines (cloud APIs, existing discovery tools, webhooks).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Reconciliation rules to deduplicate and merge sources.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Health scoring visible on the canvas (e.g., node color/opacity based on freshness/completeness).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Consider LLM-assisted pattern learning for discovery if you're building connectors.</li>
</ul><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Many CMDB projects fail here—not the UI.</p></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">Agent Orchestration &amp; Specialization</strong>
Having plugins expose specialized agents is powerful, but coordination matters. Think about:</p><ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">A central agent router/orchestrator that decides which specialized agent(s) to invoke based on intent and context from the graph.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Tool-calling patterns so agents can query the GraphQL layer, read canvas state, or trigger plugin actions.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Guardrails: audit logs, approval workflows for high-impact actions (changes, especially), and human-in-the-loop escalation.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Multi-agent teams (e.g., incident agent calls knowledge agent + change simulator).</li>
</ul><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">This is where true agentic value emerges—proactive suggestions like "This incident impacts these 7 services—simulate outage?" directly from the canvas.</p></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">UX Polish &amp; Accessibility</strong></p><ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Canvas as default landing: Great for power users/explorers, but ensure quick entry points for casual users (e.g., search bar that jumps to relevant subgraph, saved views, or default "my services" dashboard).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Dock/apps: Make it feel responsive and customizable (pin/unpin, reorder). Mobile/tablet support will matter for broader adoption.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Chat enhancements: Streaming responses, suggested prompts based on canvas selection, voice input, or deep linking (click a node → auto-populate chat context).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Dark/light mode, keyboard navigation everywhere, and accessibility for nodes/edges.</li>
</ul></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">Technical Architecture Tips</strong></p><ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">GraphQL layer</strong>: Use federation if plugins grow into separate services (subgraphs composed into a supergraph). This keeps the CMDB core stable while plugins evolve independently.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Real-time</strong>: Subscriptions for live updates (new relationships, status changes) so the canvas reflects changes without refresh.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Auth &amp; Permissions</strong>: Row-level or graph-traversal security is crucial—users should only see CIs/relationships they’re authorized for.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Backend</strong>: Ensure the CMDB supports efficient graph queries (consider Neo4j or similar under the hood if relationships dominate, with GraphQL on top).</li>
</ul></li>
</ol>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">How This Stacks Against the 2026 Landscape</h3>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">You're building something more opinionated and delightful than most alternatives:</p>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">AI-native players (Rezolve.ai, Atomicwork, Thunai, Salesforce Agentforce) emphasize agentic workflows and conversational interfaces, but few center on a beautiful, interactive graph canvas as the core experience.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Traditional competitors focus on faster/cheaper ITSM but rarely feel as "desktop-app modern" with a pluggable dock.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Your combination—visual graph baseline + chat-orchestrated specialized agents + extensible plugins—could deliver faster time-to-value and higher stickiness, especially for teams that value exploration and proactive insights over pure ticketing.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">The risk is still data accuracy and proving enterprise-grade reliability (scale, compliance, integrations). Start by nailing a few high-value flows end-to-end (e.g., "Investigate this service → spot risky dependencies → propose change" entirely via chat + canvas).</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">What’s next on your roadmap? Are you focusing on discovery/integration first, deepening the agent capabilities, or polishing the ReactFlow/dock experience? Any specific pain points you’re hitting in the MVP (e.g., graph perf, agent context passing, plugin isolation)? I’d love to dive deeper on architecture patterns, agent design, or even specific ReactFlow optimizations if helpful. This has real legs—keep pushing the conversational + visual angle.</p></div></div><section class="inline-media-container flex flex-col gap-1 clear-both"></section></div></div><div class="order-first max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">That's a critical phase—<strong class="font-semibold">tests at 100% coverage</strong> will give you confidence as you scale the APIs and tackle discovery. The discovery problem is indeed one of the hardest (and most make-or-break) parts of any CMDB. Traditional approaches often fail at scale in dynamic/hybrid/cloud environments because they rely on rigid schemas or manual mapping. Your <strong class="font-semibold">AI-first, GraphQL, pluggable architecture</strong> gives you a real opportunity to do something smarter and more maintainable.</p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Two Main Approaches You're Considering</h3>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Here's a clear breakdown:</p>
<ol dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Ingest as flexible documents + tags → Inference engine maps later</strong><ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Raw discovery data (JSON from cloud APIs, scans, agents, etc.) lands in a document store or event stream with rich metadata/tags (source, timestamp, raw attributes, provenance).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">An <strong class="font-semibold">inference/reconciliation layer</strong> (LLM-powered or rule + ML hybrid) then classifies CIs, deduplicates, enriches attributes, and builds/infers relationships.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Pros: Extremely flexible for custom or unknown CI types. Handles schema evolution gracefully. Your chat agents and plugins can help with ambiguous cases ("This looks like a new microservice—suggest classification?"). Supports "self-healing" data quality over time.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Cons: Higher latency for fresh data in the graph/canvas. Risk of inference drift or hallucinations if not grounded well. Requires strong observability on the inference pipeline.</li>
</ul></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Build the map in the discovery pipeline</strong><ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">During ingestion, apply deterministic rules, patterns, or lightweight models to immediately create/normalize CIs and relationships, then write directly to your core CMDB graph.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Pros: Faster "source of truth" updates. Better for real-time canvas refreshes and high-confidence actions (e.g., impact simulation). Aligns with mature tools like ServiceNow's probes/sensors or Device42-style agentless mapping.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Cons: Brittle for truly custom or rapidly evolving environments. Custom app architectures explode in complexity here—every new CI class or relationship type needs pipeline updates, which fights your pluggable plugin model.</li>
</ul></li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;"><strong class="font-semibold">My recommendation for your setup: Hybrid, leaning toward flexible ingestion + smart inference, with deterministic fallbacks.</strong></p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Recommended Architecture for Discovery in Your System</h3>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Ingestion Layer (Flexible Entry Point)</strong>:
Accept raw payloads via webhooks, scheduled pulls (AWS/GCP/Azure APIs, Kubernetes, SNMP, SSH, etc.), or lightweight agents. Store initially in a raw/event store (e.g., Kafka + S3/JSONB in Postgres, or a document DB). Tag everything heavily: <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">source=aws-ec2</span>, <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">timestamp</span>, <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">raw_id</span>, <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">observed_attributes</span>, <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">provenance</span>.
This keeps your core CMDB clean and supports auditing/replay.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Normalization &amp; Reconciliation Pipeline</strong>:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Deterministic first pass</strong>: Use identification rules (similar to ServiceNow IRE) based on strong keys (instance ID, serial, MAC, unique cloud ARN, etc.) to deduplicate and merge basic attributes. Define "authoritative sources" per attribute type (e.g., cloud API wins on IP/tags, monitoring wins on health).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Inference/augmentation layer</strong>: Feed normalized docs to an <strong class="font-semibold">inference engine</strong> for:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">CI classification (especially custom or new types).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Relationship inference (e.g., "depends_on", "runs_on", "part_of_service") using patterns, graph traversal, or LLM-as-judge with your CMDB context.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Enrichment (ownership, business context, risk scores).
Leverage your existing <strong class="font-semibold">OpenAI integration</strong> here—specialized agents can review batches or edge cases. For speed/cost, combine with smaller models or rule engines (e.g., via code or a lightweight ML layer).</li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Core CMDB Graph Layer</strong>:
Once reconciled, materialize into your persistent graph model (Neo4j, PostgreSQL with graph extensions, or a graph-aware store). This is what ReactFlow queries and plugins consume. Use <strong class="font-semibold">GraphQL mutations</strong> with strict validation for writes to maintain integrity.
Support dynamic/custom CI types via extensible schemas (e.g., base <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">CI</span> type + extensions for attributes/relationships). Plugins can register their own CI subclasses or relationship types.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Feedback Loops for Self-Improvement</strong>:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Canvas users or chat agents flag bad data → triggers re-inference or human review.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Monitor staleness, completeness, and relationship accuracy with health scores visible on nodes.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Periodic reconciliation jobs sweep for drift.</li>
</ul></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">This hybrid avoids the rigidity that kills many custom CMDBs while still giving you reliable, real-time-ish data for the visual canvas and agents.</p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Handling Custom App Architectures &amp; Pluggability</h3>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Your dock + plugins model is a strength here. Don't make discovery a monolithic pipeline. Instead:</p>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Plugins (incident, change, etc.) can <strong class="font-semibold">contribute</strong> to discovery rules or inference prompts. For example, a "cloud" plugin registers AWS/GCP connectors and classification logic.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Use <strong class="font-semibold">GraphQL federation</strong> (subgraphs) so each plugin owns its slice of the schema while the core CMDB subgraph handles shared CIs/relationships. This keeps the system composable without explosion. The supergraph stays stable for your ReactFlow and chat layers.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">For truly custom apps: Allow declarative extensions—users/admins define new CI classes + attributes via a low-code interface or YAML, then the inference engine learns to handle them. This is where AI shines over rigid traditional models.</li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Practical Next Steps After API Tests</h3>
<ol dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Prioritize core connectors</strong> — Start with high-value ones: major cloud providers (via APIs), Kubernetes, basic network scans. Build a generic "discovery adapter" interface so plugins can plug in easily.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Implement identification &amp; reconciliation rules early</strong> — Even simple ones prevent duplicates. Test with synthetic messy data.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Prototype the inference piece small</strong> — Use your chat/LLM setup to classify a batch of raw docs and suggest relationships. Measure accuracy and cost.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Real-time vs. batch</strong> — For canvas reactivity, use subscriptions on the reconciled graph. Heavy inference can run async with eventual consistency.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Data quality as a feature</strong> — Expose discovery health in the ReactFlow UI (node opacity/color for freshness/confidence). Let agents proactively say "I see potential drift on these 12 CIs—review?"</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">This approach keeps complexity manageable while playing to your AI/chat strengths. Pure "build map in pipeline" works for static environments but will frustrate you with custom apps. Pure "documents forever" delays value in the visual layer.</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">What does your current data model look like for CIs and relationships (e.g., relational DB, graph DB, or something else under the GraphQL layer)? Are you targeting mostly cloud-native environments, hybrid, or on-prem heavy? Any specific discovery sources you're starting with (AWS, K8s, etc.)? That would help refine this further.</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">You're building something that could genuinely feel more alive and adaptive than legacy CMDBs—keep going on the tests, then this layer will unlock the real magic for agents and the canvas.</p></div></div><section class="inline-media-container flex flex-col gap-1 max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">That's a <strong class="font-semibold">smart move</strong>—integrating <strong class="font-semibold">Provara</strong> as your central LLM gateway aligns perfectly with the pluggable, AI-first architecture you're building.</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">By routing all model calls through Provara (via its <strong class="font-semibold">OpenAI v1-compatible</strong> <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">/v1/chat/completions</span> endpoint), you solve several pain points at once:</p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Key Benefits for Your Platform</h3>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Single API key per plugin</strong>: Plugins (incident agent, change simulator, knowledge retriever, discovery inference, etc.) only need to know one base URL + one Provara token. No more juggling dozens of provider keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, xAI, Ollama, etc.) across modules. This keeps plugin code clean and secure.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Centralized model management</strong>: You (or admins) register/configure models once in Provara. Plugins can request models by name (e.g., <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">"gpt-4o"</span>, <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">"claude-3-5-sonnet"</span>, or even a custom alias like <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">"fast-reasoning"</span>). Provara handles the rest.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Adaptive intelligence out of the box</strong>: Provara doesn't just proxy—it learns from responses. It classifies requests by task/complexity, routes to the best-performing/cost-effective model per cell, detects silent regressions, and auto-migrates to cheaper models when quality parity is confirmed. For your use cases this is gold:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Simple chat triage or quick canvas queries → cheaper/faster models automatically.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Heavy reasoning (impact simulation, relationship inference, custom CI classification) → higher-quality models.</li>
</ul></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Cost control &amp; observability</strong>: Budget hard-stops, quality-adjusted spend tracking, per-user/token attribution, and dashboards. In an enterprise CMDB/service platform, this prevents surprise bills as agent usage grows. You also get audit logs and compliance-friendly features (tenant scoping, SIEM integration).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Self-host or cloud flexibility</strong>: You can run Provara self-hosted (Docker compose) alongside your backend for full control and data privacy—important for enterprise customers wary of sending sensitive CMDB data (service maps, incidents, configs) to external providers.</li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">How This Fits Your Architecture</h3>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Chat interface &amp; agents</strong>: Your Ctrl+K chat (and specialized @agents from plugins) can continue using the OpenAI SDK or direct POSTs—just point the baseURL to Provara. Context passing (selected nodes from ReactFlow, graph queries, etc.) stays the same.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Inference engine for discovery</strong>: Perfect fit. Raw discovery documents can be sent to Provara-routed models for classification, deduplication suggestions, or relationship inference. You could even expose a lightweight "inference" endpoint in your GraphQL layer that internally calls Provara with the right model and prompt templates.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Plugins</strong>: Each plugin registers its specialized agents/tools once. They call Provara uniformly. If a plugin needs a domain-specific model (e.g., a coding-focused one for change risk analysis), it can request it by name while Provara optimizes routing behind the scenes.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">ReactFlow canvas &amp; core CMDB</strong>: Any AI-powered features (auto-layout suggestions, anomaly highlighting, proactive health insights) benefit from consistent, observable LLM access.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">This keeps your system <strong class="font-semibold">composable</strong> without turning model management into a sprawl. Plugins stay focused on domain logic (ITSM workflows, graph mutations, etc.), while Provara owns the "how do we call LLMs reliably and cheaply" problem.</p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Implementation Tips</h3>
<ol dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Quick integration</strong>:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">In your backend/services, create a thin LLM client wrapper that uses Provara's base URL + token.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">For frontend chat: Update the OpenAI client initialization similarly (if using the JS SDK).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Example (Node/TS):<div dir="auto" class="not-prose"><div class="relative not-prose </ul></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Model strategy</strong>:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Start with a few defaults: one fast/cheap for general chat, one strong for reasoning/inference, one local (Ollama via Provara) for sensitive data.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Use Provara's adaptive routing heavily—it will improve over time as your agents generate more traffic.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Add fallback logic in your app layer if needed (e.g., critical actions always require a minimum quality tier).</li>
</ul></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Discovery tie-in</strong>:
With Provara in place, your inference engine becomes much easier. You can send batches of normalized discovery docs to a dedicated "classification" model call, get structured JSON back (CI type, attributes, suggested relationships), then reconcile into your graph. Provara's regression detection helps ensure the inference quality doesn't silently degrade when providers update models.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Security &amp; governance</strong>:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Use Provara's tenant scoping and audit logs.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Add content guardrails at the gateway or in your wrapper (e.g., block prompts containing sensitive PII if needed).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">For self-hosted Provara: Deploy it in the same cluster/VPC as your CMDB backend for minimal latency and no external data egress.</li>
</ul></li>
</ol>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Potential Gotchas</h3>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Latency</strong>: Adaptive routing adds a tiny bit of overhead (classification + routing decision), but it's usually negligible compared to actual model inference. Monitor it during load testing.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Quality judge</strong>: Provara uses LLM-as-judge + user feedback. Seed it with some labeled examples from your domain (e.g., good vs. bad CMDB inference outputs) to bootstrap accuracy faster.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Self-host vs. cloud</strong>: For MVP/testing, Provara's cloud might be convenient. For production/enterprise sales, self-hosted gives you stronger data residency arguments.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Overall, this is a high-leverage integration. It reduces operational complexity, improves reliability and cost-efficiency of all your AI features, and makes the entire platform feel more "enterprise-ready" without you having to build a gateway from scratch.</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Have you already connected Provara in the MVP, or is this the next step? Do you plan to self-host it, or start with their cloud? Any specific models or use cases (e.g., for discovery inference vs. chat) you're prioritizing first? I can help brainstorm the wrapper code, prompt patterns for discovery, or how to expose model choices safely to plugins/admins.</p></div></div><section class="inline-media-container flex flex-col max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">That's excellent synergy—owning both <strong class="font-semibold">Provara</strong> (LLM gateway) and <strong class="font-semibold">Pathlight</strong> (AI agent debugger/observability) gives you a powerful, end-to-end internal stack for building reliable specialized agents in your CMDB platform.</p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">How Pathlight Complements Your Architecture</h3>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Pathlight is a <strong class="font-semibold">debugger and observability tool</strong> purpose-built for AI agents. It lets you instrument agent code with traces and spans (similar to OpenTelemetry but agent-aware), set live breakpoints where you can pause execution, inspect/edit the current state as JSON, modify prompts on the fly, and replay LLM calls directly against real models. It also supports trace diffing (compare runs side-by-side for regressions in output, latency, or cost), Git-linked traces for regression detection across commits, and CI-ready evaluations.</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Key strengths for your use case:</p>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Debugging complex agent behavior</strong>: Your specialized agents (e.g., discovery inference agent, incident triage agent, change risk simulator, relationship mapper) will involve multi-step reasoning, GraphQL queries, ReactFlow context, tool calls, and Provara-routed model calls. Pathlight makes it practical to step through these without endless <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">console.log</span> or external playgrounds.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Live iteration</strong>: Set <span class="text-sm px-1 rounded-sm !font-mono bg-orange-400/10 text-orange-500 dark:bg-orange-300/10 dark:text-orange-300">await tl.breakpoint()</span> inside an agent at critical points (e.g., after inferring a relationship from raw discovery data, or before proposing a change). Pause, tweak the state or prompt, and resume—perfect for refining inference logic or handling ambiguous CMDB data.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Regression safety</strong>: Before deploying a prompt tweak or new agent version, compare traces to ensure quality/cost doesn't degrade. Tie this to your Git workflow for confidence.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Self-hosted &amp; lightweight</strong>: Runs locally via Docker Compose with a SQLite backend—easy to run alongside your MVP backend, Provara instance, and dashboard. Cross-language (TS + Python) fits if plugins use mixed stacks.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">OpenTelemetry compatibility</strong>: If your backend or agents already use OTEL, you can feed traces into Pathlight with minimal changes.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">It pairs beautifully with <strong class="font-semibold">Provara</strong>:</p>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Provara handles routing, model selection, cost control, and adaptive quality for all LLM calls.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Pathlight gives you deep visibility and control over how agents use those calls—trace every span, replay with different models routed via Provara, or debug routing decisions indirectly through prompt/state inspection.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Together: Plugins register one Provara key → agents call models uniformly → Pathlight instruments and debugs the full execution flow.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">This combo reduces the usual agent development friction (flaky prompts, non-deterministic outputs, hard-to-reproduce bugs) and helps you ship more robust specialized agents faster.</p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Practical Integration Recommendations</h3>
<ol dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Instrument Your Agents Early</strong>:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Wrap your central agent orchestrator and plugin agents with Pathlight SDK traces/spans.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Example pattern (TypeScript, assuming your chat/agent backend):<div dir="auto" <li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Do the same for discovery inference: trace raw doc → classification → relationship suggestion → reconciliation steps.</li>
</ul></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Discovery Inference Workflow with Pathlight + Provara</strong>:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Ingest raw discovery → normalize → send batch to a "classification" agent via Provara.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Use Pathlight breakpoints to inspect inferred CI types/relationships in tricky cases (e.g., custom apps or ambiguous cloud resources).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Replay problematic spans with prompt tweaks until the inference stabilizes, then lock it in.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Add CI evaluations: Write assertions on traces (e.g., "relationship confidence &gt; 0.8" or "no hallucinated attributes") so regressions block deploys.</li>
</ul></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">For the Broader Platform</strong>:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Chat interface</strong>: Trace full user sessions (Ctrl+K queries → agent routing → specialized agent handoff → canvas updates).</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">ReactFlow canvas interactions</strong>: When a user selects nodes and asks the chat something, include that context in traces for easier debugging of context-passing bugs.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Plugin extensibility</strong>: Provide a lightweight Pathlight wrapper in your plugin SDK so third-party or internal plugin authors get great debugging out of the box.</li>
</ul></li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal"><strong class="font-semibold">Self-Hosting Setup</strong>:<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Run Pathlight collector + dashboard via Docker Compose next to Provara and your GraphQL backend.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">In production/enterprise deployments, you can run it per-tenant or centrally with proper isolation.</li>
</ul></li>
</ol>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Potential Limitations &amp; Tips</h3>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">Pathlight is excellent at <strong class="font-semibold">debugging and observability</strong>, not at high-level agent orchestration or defining agent workflows (no built-in DSL or multi-agent coordinator like some frameworks). You'll still layer it on top of your existing agent logic (or a lightweight framework if needed). Start simple: instrument the high-value paths first (discovery inference, incident/change agents).</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">It shines most once you have agents that are complex enough to be hard to debug manually—which sounds like exactly where you're heading.</p>
<h3 dir="auto" class="font-semibold text-xl max-md:font-display max-md:text-[19px] max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:tracking-[0px] max-md:mb-3 max-md:mt-3">Suggested Next Steps</h3>
<ul dir="auto" class="marker:text-secondary">
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Set up Pathlight locally (Docker compose) and instrument one existing agent (maybe the discovery classifier or a simple triage flow) this week while you're still deep in tests.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Combine with Provara: Ensure every LLM span in Pathlight records the model name/alias used via Provara so you can correlate routing decisions with behavior.</li>
<li class="break-words whitespace-pre-wrap [&amp;&gt;ul]:whitespace-normal [&amp;&gt;ol]:whitespace-normal">Add a "debug mode" toggle in your admin/dock interface that enables more verbose Pathlight tracing for power users or during onboarding.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">This ownership of Provara + Pathlight is a real differentiator—it lets you build agents that are not only powerful but observable, debuggable, and production-reliable in ways that most competitors will struggle with.</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">How integrated is Pathlight into your current MVP so far? Are you planning to use it mainly for development/debugging, or also expose some observability (e.g., trace views) to enterprise admins? Any specific agent you're struggling with right now that Pathlight could help untangle (discovery mapping, multi-agent coordination, etc.)?</p>
<p dir="auto" class="break-words last:mb-0 max-md:leading-[155%] max-md:mb-4 max-md:last:mb-0" style="white-space: pre-wrap;">With auth, canvas, chat, dock, Provara gateway, and now Pathlight debugging in your toolkit, your stack is shaping up to be genuinely modern and defensible. Keep going—this is the kind of internal tooling advantage that compounds.</p></div></div><section class="inline-media-container flex flex-col gap-1 clear-both"></section></div></div><div Action-packed, cinematic getaway\",\"description\":\"Grabs a rope and escapes by helicopter.\"},{\"title\":\"Sunny Morning\",\"imagePrompt\":\"Warm, nostalgic 35mm film still aesthetic with a soft 1970s/early-80s pastoral-cinema vibe. Golden-hour backlight flooding the frame: rich amber/orange highlights, warm skin tones, and honey-colored grasses. Gentle film halation (soft glowing bloom around bright areas and sunlit edges), slightly lifted blacks with a mild matte fade, and smooth highlight roll-off (no harsh clipping). Medium-wide composition with the subject placed left-of-frame and lots of negative space to the right; a calm, observational, “quiet moment” tone. Shallow-to-moderate depth of field: foreground grasses softly blur into the lens, subject readable but not razor sharp, background trees softened. Naturalistic contrast, slightly low micro-contrast, creamy texture. Subtle film grain throughout (fine, organic grain), mild softness and lens character (gentle vignetting, slight flare), and a restrained color palette that leans warm gold + muted greens. Overall look: dreamy, intimate, sun-drenched, painterly realism like a still from an art-house coming-of-age film.\",\"templateType\":\"I2I\",\"postID\":\"7ad8ee24-d5d5-4688-84bb-b221cddc5dd7\",\"description\":\"Warm golden-hour morning scene with film
